question: What is a poultice primarily made of?

options.A: A dry powder swallowed with plenty of water
options.B: A clear liquid injected directly into a vein
options.C: A soft, moist mass spread on a cloth
options.D: A hard plastic shell strapped onto a broken bone

explanation: A poultice consists of a moist, soft mixture applied externally using a piece of cloth or gauze. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why should a hospital nurse understand traditional poultice remedies used by patients?

options.A: To legally fine patients who use herbs at home
options.B: To safely integrate patient habits with modern medical care
options.C: To replace all prescription drugs with local leaves
options.D: To prove that traditional methods never work

explanation: Knowing what patients apply at home helps nurses prevent harmful skin reactions and manage treatments safely. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is the primary local physical effect of applying warmth via a poultice?

options.C: Complete blockage of local blood flow

explanation: Warmth causes local blood vessels to widen, bringing more blood and immune cells to the area. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h2)

question: How does increased blood flow help an infected, swollen area under a poultice?

options.A: It dries out all body fluids completely
options.B: It cools down the fever instantly
options.C: It brings white blood cells to fight the infection
options.D: It stops the heart from pumping too fast

explanation: Extra blood circulation delivers necessary white blood cells and nutrients to heal inflamed or infected tissue. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which type of poultice is commonly used to retain heat for deep inflammation and boils?
explanation: Kaolin is a heavy clay substance known for holding heat well to treat deep-seated swelling and boils. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h3)

question: A patient uses crushed fresh leaves on a swollen joint. What kind of poultice is this?
explanation: Using fresh plants or leaves directly falls under the category of traditional herbal poultices. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which condition is a clear indication for using a warm poultice?

options.B: A brand new ankle sprain with active bleeding
options.C: A localized boil or deep muscle ache
options.D: An area of skin with complete loss of sensation

explanation: Poultices work best on localized aches, stiffness, and closed infections like boils. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why should a nurse NOT apply a warm poultice to a fresh injury that happened ten minutes ago?

options.A: It turns the skin completely white permanently
options.B: It freezes the tissue and causes gangrene
options.C: It cures the injury too fast for proper charting
options.D: It increases local blood flow and worsens bleeding

explanation: Heat causes blood vessels to open up, which increases bleeding and swelling immediately after a fresh trauma. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h4)

question: What tool should the nurse use to check if a warm poultice is safe to apply?

options.A: A heavy weight pressed onto the mixture
options.B: A metal needle poked into the patient's arm
options.C: Their own inner wrist or a thermometer
options.D: A bright flashlight held close to the paste

explanation: Testing the temperature on the sensitive inner wrist helps verify the poultice is warm, not burning hot. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h5)

question: Why is a clean cloth or gauze used between the skin and the poultice paste?

options.A: To keep the application neat and hold the paste together
options.B: To cure the infection without using any medicine
options.C: To completely block all heat from reaching the patient
options.D: To prevent the nurse from wearing clean gloves

explanation: The cloth acts as a barrier that contains the messy paste while allowing warmth and medicinal properties to pass through. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the very first practical safety step before applying a prepared warm poultice to a patient?

options.A: Wrap the entire body in thick blankets
options.B: Test the temperature of the mixture
options.C: Leave the room for thirty minutes
options.D: Scrub the skin hard with stiff wire wool

explanation: Always test the temperature to prevent accidental burns before the substance touches the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h6)

question: A nurse has just placed a warm poultice on a patient's leg. When is the best time to check the skin underneath for irritation?

options.A: Only when the patient is discharged home
options.B: Never, once it is tied down it must stay
options.C: After twenty-four hours have passed completely
options.D: Within the first five minutes of application

explanation: Checking the skin early helps catch burning or allergic reactions before severe tissue damage occurs. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h6)

question: What should the nurse do immediately if a patient complains of severe burning under a poultice?

options.A: Wait another hour to see if it stops
options.B: Tie the bandage tighter to stop the burning
options.C: Tell the patient to endure the pain
options.D: Remove the poultice and wash the skin

explanation: Severe burning means the application is too hot or irritating, requiring immediate removal to prevent skin injury. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h7)

question: Why is regular skin monitoring necessary while a poultice is in place?

options.A: To catch early signs of thermal burns or irritation
options.B: To measure how much weight the patient gained
options.C: To see if the bandages can be sold again
options.D: To check if the patient is sleeping soundly

explanation: Frequent checks ensure that heat or active ingredients do not damage or blister the skin. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h7)

question: What is maceration in the context of skin care?

options.A: Skin becoming completely numb to all touch
options.B: Skin turning completely black from cold temperatures
options.C: Skin growing extra thick layers like a hard shell
options.D: Skin becoming soft and broken down from too much moisture

explanation: Maceration happens when moisture stays on the skin too long, making the tissue weak and prone to damage. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h8)

question: Which complication can happen if an unsterile herbal poultice is placed over a minor skin scratch?

options.A: Instant healing of all body aches
options.D: A permanent change in eye color

explanation: Unclean mixtures can carry germs straight into breaks in the skin, causing new infections instead of curing them. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h8)
